hero.headline: Bomb threat forces evacuation at Indian River State College in Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: Police evacuated three buildings at IRSC's Massey Campus on Friday morning after a staff member opened a threatening email. No explosives were found, and the FBI is now tracing the email's origin.
hero.body:
Police evacuated three buildings at Indian River State College's Massey Campus in Fort Pierce on Friday morning after a bomb threat was emailed to the campus, though no explosives were found. A staff member opened the email shortly before 9 a.m. and immediately notified campus security, according to Fort Pierce police.

 Officers evacuated three buildings identified in the message, including the library, and conducted thorough searches. St. Lucie police and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office assisted in the search. Barbara Rubin-Perry, who was inside the college at the time, said she was really scared more than anybody else there.

 Police said the email appears similar in format to threats reported in Martin County on Thursday, though they cannot directly connect the incidents. The FBI is now working with local investigators to trace the email's origin.

 Michael Santiago of the Fort Pierce Police Department said such threats disrupt classes and divert officers from other duties. "We're disrupting a school, all of the students, all of the faculty. So once we narrow this down, for those who are making these threats, we will find you and we will prosecute you," Santiago said.

 He added that police dedicate significant resources to these threats because they never know if one might be real. The campus is expected to resume normal operations on Monday.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after deputies find 8 suspected explosive devices at home
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man Thursday after deputies serving a risk protection order found eight suspected explosive devices and bomb-making materials at his home near Balsam Drive.

Deputies with the Targeted Violence Unit went to the residence at about 12:20 p.m. Thursday to serve the risk protection order when they identified numerous suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians removed seven suspected destructive devices from the home and placed them in a containment vessel. After obtaining a search warrant, deputies found and safely removed an eighth suspected explosive device, along with a large quantity of materials used to make explosive devices. Eight firearms were also seized from the home as part of the risk protection order.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to threats. Del Toro praised the Targeted Violence Unit detectives for recognizing the potential danger and taking immediate action, and the Bomb Disposal Team technicians for putting themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove the devices. Del Toro said he is grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as the investigation continues.

Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, was charged with eight counts of possessing, making or attempting to make a destructive device. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond. The investigation remains ongoing. The sheriff's office said there is no immediate threat to the community.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport adds dual baggage claim gates in $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed its $3 million renovation with dual baggage claim gates allowing passengers to retrieve bags within 100 feet of aircraft arrival, along with covered walkways and a new courtyard.
cards.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed a $3 million renovation project that includes dual baggage claim gates, covered walkways, a new courtyard and canopies over passenger areas. The upgrades, which also feature a turf patio and redesigned baggage claim area, drew praise from travelers who described significantly improved conditions compared to the previous facility.

 Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the new baggage claim system allows passengers to pick up their bags within 100 feet of where the aircraft arrives. The renovations include a new courtyard with seating where passengers can wait for their flights, along with canopies over the passenger walkways and baggage claim areas.

 Passenger Austin Garafola described the improvements, saying it is definitely a lot better and passengers now go right in under the awning instead of waiting in single file and getting rained on. Passenger Doris Newell said the facility and accessibility are great and wonderful.

 The airport serves three commercial airlines: American, JetBlue and Breeze. Airport officials announced plans for a concession area for departing passengers, and new long-term parking has been approved. The airport also plans to invite the community this fall to weigh in on potential designs for a terminal expansion. Dambeck said the changes create a better experience for passengers as they wait for their flights.

cards.teaser: Drivers should expect multiple overnight I-95 ramp closures around Kanner Highway, High Meadow Avenue, Becker Road and Gatlin Boulevard, along with lane closures on major roads in Martin and St. Lucie counties.
cards.body:
Drivers across the Treasure Coast should prepare for a busy week of construction impacts beginning Sunday, Sept. 13, with multiple I-95 ramp closures, overnight lane closures and local-road restrictions scheduled in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

 The Florida Department of Transportation's Sept. 11-18 traffic report lists some of the most significant impacts around Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue in Martin County and Becker Road and Gatlin Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. Several closures have contingency dates in case weather or other conditions delay the work.

Two northbound lanes are scheduled to close from 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. over the same period.

 I-95 northbound entrance ramp from Kanner Highway: The ramp is scheduled to close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Wednesday, Sept. 16. Traffic will be directed south on Kanner Highway, then to Pratt Whitney Road and east on Bridge Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp. Thursday, Sept. 17, is listed as the contingency date.

hero.headline: Bomb threat forces evacuation at Indian River State College in Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: Police evacuated three buildings at IRSC's Massey Campus on Friday morning after a staff member opened a threatening email. No explosives were found, and the FBI is now tracing the email's origin.
hero.body:
Police evacuated three buildings at Indian River State College's Massey Campus in Fort Pierce on Friday morning after a bomb threat was emailed to the campus, though no explosives were found. A staff member opened the email shortly before 9 a.m. and immediately notified campus security, according to Fort Pierce police.

 Officers evacuated three buildings identified in the message, including the library, and conducted thorough searches. St. Lucie police and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office assisted in the search. Barbara Rubin-Perry, who was inside the college at the time, said she was really scared more than anybody else there.

 Police said the email appears similar in format to threats reported in Martin County on Thursday, though they cannot directly connect the incidents. The FBI is now working with local investigators to trace the email's origin.

 Michael Santiago of the Fort Pierce Police Department said such threats disrupt classes and divert officers from other duties. "We're disrupting a school, all of the students, all of the faculty. So once we narrow this down, for those who are making these threats, we will find you and we will prosecute you," Santiago said.

 He added that police dedicate significant resources to these threats because they never know if one might be real. The campus is expected to resume normal operations on Monday.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport adds dual baggage claim gates in $3 million renovation
hero.teaser: Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed its $3 million renovation with dual baggage claim gates allowing passengers to retrieve bags within 100 feet of aircraft arrival, along with covered walkways and a new courtyard.
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed a $3 million renovation project that includes dual baggage claim gates, covered walkways, a new courtyard and canopies over passenger areas. The upgrades, which also feature a turf patio and redesigned baggage claim area, drew praise from travelers who described significantly improved conditions compared to the previous facility.

 Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the new baggage claim system allows passengers to pick up their bags within 100 feet of where the aircraft arrives. The renovations include a new courtyard with seating where passengers can wait for their flights, along with canopies over the passenger walkways and baggage claim areas.

 Passenger Austin Garafola described the improvements, saying it is definitely a lot better and passengers now go right in under the awning instead of waiting in single file and getting rained on. Passenger Doris Newell said the facility and accessibility are great and wonderful.

 The airport serves three commercial airlines: American, JetBlue and Breeze. Airport officials announced plans for a concession area for departing passengers, and new long-term parking has been approved. The airport also plans to invite the community this fall to weigh in on potential designs for a terminal expansion. Dambeck said the changes create a better experience for passengers as they wait for their flights.
